source.title: LiteTransformerSearch: Training-free On-device Search for Efficient Autoregressive Language Models
source.authors: Mojan Javaheripi; Gustavo de Rosa; Subhabrata Mukherjee; S. Shah; T. Religa; C. Mendes; Sébastien Bubeck; F. Koushanfar; Debadeepta Dey

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how parameter count relates to trained-model perplexity and directly tests topology variation at a fixed decoder parameter count, using rank correlation and perplexity deviation rather than fitting the original scaling-law curves.
record.gate_note: The study does not fit power laws or test extrapolation from small runs, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or scaling predictions for downstream tasks. Its training-free proxy results are measurements of parameter-count/perplexity ranking, not power-law exponent estimates. The downstream results compare selected LTS models with OPT-350M but do not relate downstream performance to scale or pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: A NAS paper, but it reports its own fully trained results on two claim parts. Across 200+ randomly sampled GPT-2 and Transformer-XL architectures, validation perplexity ranks closely with non-embedding (decoder) parameter count. At fixed decoder parameter count, width-to-depth aspect ratio changes perplexity little (Sec. 4.3, App. E), echoing Kaplan's Fig. 5. The method differs: rank correlation and deviation from the median, not power-law fits.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that decoder (non-embedding) parameter count is a zero-cost, accurate proxy for ranking autoregressive Transformer perplexity, regardless of topology within their search space. Topology strongly affects latency and memory but changes perplexity little at a fixed decoder parameter count, except for very deep models.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce scaling-law curve fits; it tests a training-free parameter-count ranking proxy on trained architectures and compares perplexity across topology choices.
record.method_sensitivity: Parameter-count definition matters: embedding parameters can mask the ranking relationship. Very deep Transformer-XL models and GPT-2 models near aspect ratio 1 show increased perplexity. Per-architecture learning-rate tuning changes the reported correlation from 0.96 to 0.93, although the paper says rankings remain largely unchanged.

fits_no_version.finding: Encoder-only BERT encoder and total parameter counts rank test perplexity with SRC 0.96 and 0.98.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter count ranks perplexity for sampled encoder-only Transformers.

fits_no_version.finding: In an NMT benchmark, parameter count vs BLEU/perplexity correlation varies by language pair and is inverse for low-resource so-en and sw-en.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In low-data translation pairs, larger models may perform worse.

fits_no_version.finding: LTS-selected ~300–420M-decoder-parameter models beat OPT-350M on average zero/one-shot accuracy with lower latency.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Not a scaling claim; the study's own method compared with a baseline.

record.problems: The central scaling-related evidence is rank correlation and reported perplexity deviations, not fitted power laws or exponents. Results use selected architecture samples and limited backbones/datasets; uncertainty estimates are not reported. Some topology results are summarized from figures, and the deep-model exceptions are stated without numerical effect sizes.

untested.parts: Power-law functional form, exponents, token and compute scaling, and range over several orders of magnitude (models span ~2–100M decoder params).
All: no small-run fit is extrapolated to larger runs.
All: no fixed-compute allocation of parameters vs tokens.
All: BERT and NMT results are rank correlations, not power-law fits.
All: downstream comparisons are LTS vs OPT-350M, not scale-vs-performance trends.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal split on setup; disagreement between published laws.

missing.what: Decoder parameter count vs fully trained perplexity for 1200 Transformer-XL models sampled during search: SRC 0.98.
Homogeneous Transformer-XL models (100): decoder param SRC 0.95 with perplexity; total param SRC low.
SRC within narrow decoder-parameter bins stays high.
Varying adaptive embedding factor k changes total params with little perplexity change.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 limits_scope label was replaced: an untested power-law form is listed under untested, not as a scope limit. The r8 V7 link was removed. The study cites Kaplan et al. as consistent with its findings; it is not an original source. All evidence is rank correlation on small models (≤~100M decoder params, ≤~420M for the Pile models).

versions.untested_parts: Tests the direction and ranking relationship between parameter count and validation perplexity, but does not fit a power law, report exponents, test token or compute scaling, or establish behavior over several orders of magnitude.
No small-run fit is used to predict the losses of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token growth law is tested.
Tests width-to-depth aspect ratio at fixed decoder parameter count for GPT-2 and Transformer-XL; does not test every architectural detail or a broad range of model families.

No other modalities, repeated-data regime, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling laws are tested. Preliminary encoder-only and encoder-decoder parameter-count ranking results do not test the same power-law claim.
Downstream accuracy is compared between LTS models and OPT-350M, but the study does not test whether downstream performance predictably improves with scale or pretraining loss.

Tests sensitivity of parameter-count ranking to total versus decoder parameter counting and to learning-rate choice, and reports deviations for deep models; it does not compare fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations across studies.

rows.subject: GPT-2
rows.size_stated: 100 randomly sampled models; 2–16 layers and 2–65M total parameters
rows.operation_detail: Compared the parameter-count/perplexity ranking under a per-architecture learning-rate sweep with the shared-learning-rate setup
rows.measure: Optimal learning rate frequency and correlation with decoder parameter count
rows.value: Optimal rate is 0.01 for 98% of architectures; per-architecture optimization gives correlation 0.93
rows.locator: Appendix B, Choice of Training Hyperparameters
rows.note: The authors say rankings remain largely unchanged after learning-rate optimization.
rows.check: A per-architecture learning-rate sweep leaves the ranking 'largely unchanged' (0.93 vs 0.96), and 98% of models share the optimal LR. This is little dependence on the training choice. Ranking measure, not exponents.

source_check.correct: Among 100 GPT-2 models with 2–16 layers and 2–65M total parameters, 98% select learning rate 0.01. Correlation is 0.93 after per-architecture optimization versus 0.96 with the shared rate. V7 state: cannot_determine; fitted exponents and compute-optimal allocation are not tested.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix B, Choice of Training Hyperparameters, lines 888–898.
source_check.problem: Little change in ranking cannot establish absence of setup dependence in fitted exponents or allocation.
